newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT -JGBs seen mired in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -JGBs seen mired in directionless trade.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to be stuck near the previous day's range in directionless trade on Friday, with the market lacking fresh trading incentives, traders said.
"After the sharp fall on Wednesday, JGBs pared some of the losses (on Thursday) and now seem to be caught in a lull," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
Although JGBs may be supported by investor buying of cash bonds on dips, a dearth of fresh buying factors is likely to preclude a convincing break above 124.00 during the day, traders said.
Some investors were able to buy recently auctioned 10-year JGBs cheaply after Wednesday's sharp fall, the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
But they are unlikely to bid aggressively for cash JGBs on the upside, he said.
The price of the new 10-year JGB issue fell by about one yen after Wednesday's decline, traders said.
Buy-backs ahead of the forward shift in the benchmark contract from June to September may also provide some support, a brokerage house trader said.
The June contract, however, is likely to feel heavy on the upside, as selling pressure from traders who took long positions above 124.00 will probably weigh on the market, the first trader said.
Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka are scheduled to deliver speeches at a meeting of national credit associations due to start at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT).
